Heritage walk in Jaipur: the walled city, Amber and museums

By @archaeologywala for Talaash Heritage · Updated 15 October 2026

A heritage walk in Jaipur explores the planned walled city founded by Sawai Jai Singh II in 1727, a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2019, with Jantar Mantar (UNESCO, 2010), the City Palace and Hawa Mahal. Amber Fort, part of the Hill Forts of Rajasthan site, sits about 11 km north on the old route into the hills.

We arrange Jaipur heritage walks and study tours on request for schools, colleges, companies and private groups, with an archaeologist or historian, in English or Hindi.

Why Jaipur matters

Jaipur is one of the clearest examples of a planned early modern city in South Asia. Sawai Jai Singh II, the Kachhwaha ruler, moved his capital from the hill fortress of Amber to the plain in 1727 and laid out a grid of wide bazaars and city blocks (chowkris) inside a wall with gates. The streets, market arcades and temple plots still follow that plan.

The city is also a meeting point of Rajput and Mughal traditions. The Kachhwahas served the Mughal emperors from Akbar's time onward, and Amber and Jaipur show how Rajput courts adopted Mughal garden planning, audience halls and decoration while keeping their own temples, stepwells and palace layouts.

Layers of Jaipur's history

The Kachhwahas held Amber from about the 11th century. Raja Man Singh I, Akbar's general, began the present Amber Fort palace in the late 16th century, and Mirza Raja Jai Singh I added to it in the 17th. Jaigarh, on the ridge above, was built and rebuilt in the same period as the fortress that guarded Amber.

Sawai Jai Singh II (ruled 1699 to 1743) founded Jaipur, built the City Palace and the Jantar Mantar observatory between about 1728 and 1734, and Nahargarh on the ridge. Sawai Pratap Singh added the Hawa Mahal in 1799 so women of the court could watch street processions. The city was painted its familiar pink in the 19th century, often linked to the 1876 visit of the Prince of Wales, and Sawai Ram Singh II built the Albert Hall, now the city's main museum, in the 1880s.

The Forts of India guide places Amber in the wider story of Rajput hill forts.

Places a heritage walk in Jaipur covers

  1. Hawa Mahal 1799

    A five-storey screen of small windows facing Siredeori Bazaar; go round the back to see how thin the building really is.

  2. City Palace 1727 onward

    Royal residence with Mubarak Mahal, Diwan-i-Khas and the Pritam Niwas courtyard gates; parts are a museum.

  3. Jantar Mantar about 1728 to 1734

    Sawai Jai Singh II's observatory of masonry instruments, a UNESCO site since 2010.

  4. Tripolia Bazaar and Chaura Rasta 1727 plan

    Main grid bazaars of the walled city, with arcades and chowk junctions.

  5. Govind Dev Ji Temple 18th century

    Temple in the City Palace grounds, aligned with the palace, an example of how the plan joined court and worship.

  6. Isarlat 1749

    Tower built by Sawai Ishwari Singh near Tripolia Gate, with a view over the grid.

  7. Albert Hall Museum 1887

    Indo-Saracenic building by Samuel Swinton Jacob, housing the state museum.

  8. Amber Fort late 16th to 18th century

    Kachhwaha palace of courtyards, the Sheesh Mahal and Ganesh Pol; part of the Hill Forts of Rajasthan UNESCO site.

  9. Panna Meena ka Kund 17th century

    Stepwell near Amber with criss-cross stairs on three sides.

  10. Jaigarh Fort 17th to 18th century

    Ridge fortress above Amber with cannon foundry and large water tanks.

  11. Nahargarh Fort 1734, extended 1868

    Fort on the ridge overlooking the city; the Madhavendra Bhawan suites were added in the 19th century.

  12. Gaitore 18th to 20th century

    Royal cenotaphs (chhatris) of the Jaipur rulers below Nahargarh.

Walking routes in Jaipur

The walled city on foot

About 3 hours

Hawa Mahal → Jantar Mantar → City Palace → Govind Dev Ji Temple → Tripolia Bazaar and Chaura Rasta → Isarlat

Amber and the ridge

Half a day, by vehicle

Amber Fort → Panna Meena ka Kund → Jaigarh Fort

Museum and cenotaphs

About 3 hours, a short drive to Gaitore

Albert Hall Museum → Gaitore → Nahargarh Fort

Museums in Jaipur

  • Albert Hall Museum. Rajasthan's oldest museum, with sculpture, metalwork, textiles, paintings and an Egyptian mummy.
  • City Palace museum. Royal textiles, arms, manuscripts and paintings of the Jaipur court.
  • Amrapali Museum. Private museum of Indian jewellery and silver objects.

Best time for a walk

October to March. Walk the old city early in the morning before traffic builds; summer afternoons are very hot.

What you see on a Jaipur walk

Inside the walled city you can read the plan on the ground: straight bazaars, equal blocks, arcaded shopfronts and temples set at junctions. At Jantar Mantar the instruments are large enough to walk through, and students can measure local time with the Samrat Yantra sundial. The Jaipur Jantar Mantar programme is built around exactly this.

At Amber you move from public courtyards to private apartments, reading how a Rajput palace controls access, light and water. Panna Meena ka Kund, a stepwell near Amber, links the walk to the stepwells of India.

Jaipur for school and college groups

Jaipur works well as part of Three capitals: Delhi, Agra and Jaipur, and Forts of Rajasthan continues to Chittorgarh, Kumbhalgarh and other hill forts. Families can do The Golden Triangle with an archaeologist as a private journey.

The walled city is crowded and busy with traffic, so school groups should walk early in the morning in small batches with extra adults. Amber Fort, Jaigarh and Nahargarh need a vehicle; Jantar Mantar, the City Palace and Hawa Mahal are close together and can be walked. Check site websites for current rules before you go.

Questions people ask

Which historical places in Jaipur should a heritage walk cover?

Inside the walled city: Hawa Mahal, Jantar Mantar, the City Palace and the main bazaars. Outside: Amber Fort, Panna Meena ka Kund, Jaigarh and Nahargarh. The Albert Hall Museum is the best single museum stop.

How many UNESCO sites are there in Jaipur?

Three are linked to Jaipur: Jantar Mantar (2010), Amber Fort as part of the Hill Forts of Rajasthan (2013), and the Jaipur walled city itself (2019).

Is a Jaipur heritage walk good for school students?

Yes. Jantar Mantar is excellent for science and history together, and the City Palace and Hawa Mahal are close by. Walk early, in small groups, and use a coach for Amber and the ridge forts.

What are the main museums in Jaipur?

The Albert Hall Museum is the state museum, with collections across art and archaeology. The City Palace museum covers the royal court. Amber Fort itself works as a museum of palace architecture.

Can we combine Jaipur with Delhi and Agra?

Yes. Talaash Heritage arranges the Three capitals study tour and private journeys linking Delhi, Agra and Jaipur, led by an archaeologist or historian, in English or Hindi.
